inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has granted regular bail to a man accused under national-security provisions and the Official Secrets Act, saying suspicion alone—of sharing sensitive information with someone in Pakistan—can’t justify keeping him locked up indefinitely. The alleged contact was with Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri.” This looks less like a clear security case than a system using national-security labels to create a frightening story, then quietly stepping back when the evidence can’t support prolonged detention. Bail isn’t proof of innocence, but the accusations aren’t proof of guilt either.
